summary: Phase 2 (implement + wire the Sfor-containment loop-check) of plan 04 COMPLETE. Replaced the Phase-1 `none`-stub `intFImpReuseWitness?` in Expansion.lean with a real implementation: reads psi as newForms's sole sign=.neg entry and Sfor(w') as newForms's sign=.pos sublist, then searches (bPers.map (.label)).eraseDups via List.findSome? for the first world label x such that isAccessible edges w x, Sfor(w') subseteq posFormulasAt bPers x (via List.contains), and psi not in posFormulasAt bPers x. Wired into go's `some (.linearResult newForms nw' newEdge, newExp)` branch: matching on newEdge, the `none` (alpha-rule) sub-case is unchanged; the `some e` (world-creating F(phi->psi)) sub-case now calls intFImpReuseWitness? bPers edges newForms e -- `some x` takes the no-new-world path (bPers unchanged, edges unchanged, world counter nw unchanged/unconsumed, F(phi->psi)@w still marked expanded via newExp), `none` creates w' exactly as before (Branch.extendMany, nw', edges ++ [e]). Expansion.lean builds GREEN with zero new sorries/axioms/vacuous defs. Signature-change question: NO -- intFImpRule/intApplyRuleFull/intStepBranch signatures are all unchanged; the entire check and its wiring live inside go, exactly as the Phase 1 GO verdict predicted. Preserved-Asset check: a scoped build of the downstream Soundness module surfaced exactly one broken lemma, intExpandBranches_closed_unsat (Soundness.lean, starts line 1083; unification failures at ~1396 and ~1461) -- its induction assumed every world-creating linearResult step strictly grows the branch (via Branch.extendMany / a new edge), which the reuse (some x) path no longer does. This is the EXPECTED fallout flagged by this phase's own instructions; it was NOT patched (no weakening, no sorry added) -- it is recorded here verbatim for Phase 3 (countermodel/Hintikka re-verification) and Phase 4 (soundness audit) to resolve. Scheme.lean sorries at lines 330 and 985 are unchanged (Phase 2 closes no sorry).
signature_change_reasoning: Confirmed as predicted in Phase 1: go already carries bPers and edges (pre-extension) in its own parameter scope at the exact point the F(phi->psi) world-creating rule fires. intFImpRule, intApplyRuleFull, and intStepBranch keep their existing parameter lists unchanged. The reuse witness (intFImpReuseWitness? bPers edges newForms e) and its branch dispatch are implemented entirely inside go.

preserved_asset_fallout.diagnosis: The lemma's induction on intExpandBranches assumes that every `some (.linearResult newForms nw' (some newEdge), newExp)` step strictly extends the branch (Branch.extendMany bPers newForms) and appends the new edge. With the Sfor-containment reuse path now live, the `some x` witness case instead continues on `bPers` unchanged with `edges` unchanged and `nw` unconsumed -- a genuinely new case the induction does not yet cover.

preserved_asset_fallout.suggested_resolution_for_phase_3_or_4: Add an induction case for the reuse (`some x`) branch showing satisfiability is preserved: since Sfor(w') subseteq posFormulasAt bPers x (the ancestor x already forces everything the fresh world would have forced) and x is accessible from w, any model satisfying the branch at x also witnesses whatever `intBranchSatisfied` needs from the (never-created) w' -- no fresh `worldOf'` is needed because x already serves that role. This likely requires a monotonicity/containment lemma relating `posFormulasAt` containment to `intBranchSatisfied` preservation, analogous to the existing persistence-preservation argument.
